title: Opioid Prescribing: Sedation, Respiratory Risk and Antidotes
subject: Prescription Pearls
preview: Opioids may cause respiratory depression, drowsiness, constipation and nausea; monitor consciousness and ventilation.
quickRevision: Opioids may cause respiratory depression, drowsiness, constipation and nausea; monitor consciousness and ventilation.
Dose changes need caution with older age, sleep apnea, renal impairment and sedative co-medications.
Support airway and breathing first in suspected severe toxicity and observe for recurrence after reversal.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Opioids may cause respiratory depression, drowsiness, constipation and nausea; monitor consciousness and ventilation.
Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression but may wear off before a longer-acting opioid.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Dose changes need caution with older age, sleep apnea, renal impairment and sedative co-medications.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Normal oxygen saturation while receiving oxygen can coexist with hypoventilation.

quiz.question: Which drug is used to reverse opioid-induced respiratory depression?
quiz.explanation: Naloxone reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression but may wear off before a longer-acting opioid.
